user.title: Set up Tankpriser
user.description: Which country do you buy fuel in? One setup covers one country — if you also fill up across a border, add that country afterwards as a second Tankpriser entry.

area.title: Area & fuel types
area.description: Choose which fuels to track. Your area is Home Assistant's Home location and the radius can be changed later under Options.

data_description.anchor: German prices can only be looked up around a point, and this one has to stand still: the sensors, the history and the price notifications all compare the same stations from one update to the next. Asking out loud still searches from wherever you actually are.

credentials.title: API key
credentials.description:
This country's prices come from a source that only answers with a personal API key. It is free, and it is yours — Home Assistant sends it straight to the source and nowhere else.

{guides}

error.no_fuel_types: Select at least one fuel type.
error.key_required: This source needs a key before it can be set up.
error.invalid_auth: The source rejected that key. A brand-new key is usually not activated yet — that is done by hand and can take days. Check you copied all of it, then try again when the activation mail arrives.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the source. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.no_stations: The key was accepted but no stations came back. Please open an issue if this persists.

user.title: Add a car
user.description: Predict when this car will need refuelling from the fuel level Home Assistant already knows. The prediction is free — if you find it useful, please consider donating; it took real work to build. 💛

data_description.source_entity: The entity that reports the fuel level — a sensor, or e.g. a car device_tracker.
data_description.level_attribute: Leave empty to use the entity's state. Otherwise the attribute holding the level, e.g. fuel_level. Nested attributes use dots: data.fuel.level.
data_description.tank_capacity_l: Full tank size in litres. Used to turn a percentage into litres and to estimate range.
data_description.odometer_entity: Optional. With an odometer we predict in L/100 km; without one we fall back to a time-based estimate.
data_description.odometer_attribute: Optional. Leave empty to use the odometer entity's state, or name the attribute holding the reading.
data_description.fuel_key: Which fuel this car uses — so we can show the cheapest nearby price for it.

settings.title: Area & fuel types
settings.description: Adjust the radius around your Home location, choose fuel types and hide stations you do not care about.

data.nearby_tracker: Rank stations near this device (phone or car)
data.nearby_radius_km: How far to look for nearby stations

notifications.title: Price notifications
notifications.description: Get notified when prices change in your area.

data.fillup_enabled: Also alert when a car is low and passing somewhere cheap
data.fillup_level_pct: Alert below this much of a tank

data_description.fillup_enabled: Needs at least one car added for prediction. You are told once per low tank, not once per update — the next alert waits until the car has been filled.

chains.title: Chains & API keys
chains.description: Most sources publish their prices openly and need no setup — the Danish chains OK, Q8, F24, Shell and OIL! work out of the box. The sources below only answer with a personal API key that you must request yourself. Pick one to see how.

provider.title: {name} API key

data_description.api_key: The key is checked immediately — if the chain rejects it you will see an error here.

discounts.title: Loyalty discounts
discounts.description: Discount per chain in øre per litre, as your fuel card advertises it. Prices everywhere — sensors, the card, notifications and the cheapest-of — then show what you actually pay. Leave a chain at 0 if you have no card for it.

prediction.title: Refuel prediction
prediction.description: How the per-car refuel prediction behaves. Both settings need at least one car added, and neither affects fuel prices.

data.calibration_enabled: Learn from past predictions and correct future ones
data.accuracy_enabled: Show me how accurate the prediction has been (advanced)

data_description.calibration_enabled: After each refuel the prediction is compared with what the tank actually did. If the typical tank has been leaning the same way, over five or more of them, later predictions are nudged back — by half the measured lean, never more than 25 %. A holiday's worth of unusual tanks is ignored rather than treated as a change of habit. On by default; turn it off to see the raw model.
data_description.accuracy_enabled: Adds the tankpriser.prediction_accuracy action and lets you use the Prediction Accuracy card, which grades every tank and says whether the model is consistently off or merely noisy. Off by default — it is a tool for judging the prediction rather than a part of it.

error.invalid_auth: The chain rejected that key. Check that you copied all of it and that it has been activated.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the chain's API. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.no_stations: The key was accepted but no stations came back. The account may not have access yet, or the chain changed its format — please open an issue.

abort.no_credential_chains: No chain currently needs an API key — every supported chain publishes its prices openly.

options.any_change: Any price change in the area
options.below_threshold: When the cheapest price drops below the threshold
options.decrease_only: Only when the cheapest price decreases

options.DK: Denmark — OK, Q8, F24, Shell and OIL!, no key needed
options.DE: Germany — Tankerkönig (MTS-K), needs a free API key
